evidence_items.explanation: Bloomberg estimates that OpenAI supplied about 70% of Microsoft’s fiscal-year AI sales, using an inferred annual AI revenue total. This supports the plausibility of substantial concentration at Microsoft, but does not establish a greater-than-70% share across the three providers, near-total compute allocation, or causation; the press estimate is used because a complete primary customer-share calculation was not obtained.

metric_scope.metric: Estimated share of fiscal-year AI revenue attributable to OpenAI

evidence_items.explanation: Alphabet identifies several contributors to Cloud growth. This is material context against attributing growth predominantly to lab compute purchases, but the statement supplies neither customer revenue shares nor quantified causal contributions.

evidence_items.explanation: The announcement confirms CoreWeave’s direct commercial connection to Anthropic. Its prospective delivery language does not establish that this agreement generated the revenue growth already observed.

evidence_items.locator: Customer-list paragraph following “Today, Runpod counts 500,000 developers”
evidence_items.explanation: The report identifies a broad customer list that also includes OpenAI. Runpod therefore does not provide a clean counterexample to the connection claim, and the list does not establish dependence or revenue concentration.

unresolved_gaps: No verified, comparable realized AI revenue denominators and lab-attributable numerators were obtained for all three hyperscalers.
No comparable allocation records establish what fraction of available AI compute the labs purchased.
The Microsoft estimate depends on assumptions about annual revenue and covers only one provider.
The records do not quantify how much growth the lab purchases caused relative to other businesses and customers.
No sufficiently complete provider and customer-chain evidence establishes the universal claim about growing AI data center companies.
Several primary financial pages were inaccessible or returned insufficient text; their search snippets were not substituted for readable evidence.
The claim’s common reporting period, revenue definition and accounting basis remain unspecified.
